# EL-F13: input binding and prior-work recovery

Date: 2026-09-05. Status: completed proposal preparation, not a new experiment.

## Program adherence and prior-work recovery

This record follows the [program charter](../../../../README.md), the existing
[SCI-FRUIT prior-work record](../PRIOR_WORK.md), and the
[accepted empirical-lane bindings](ACCEPTED_INPUT_BINDINGS_R0.1.md).
Discovery started from the package and current status, then checked all later
EL-F12 design, authorization, registration and result records. No EL-F13
predecessor was present in the repository. The toltec-context skill's current
status route points to `doc/REFACTOR_STATUS.md`; that source was read in the
actual SCI-FRUIT worktree. No sibling repository or Unity access was needed.

This is a successor empirical feasibility proposal. It does not amend the
contract charter, accepted Stage A science or a frozen package. All
implementation and empirical material remains excluded from Stage B authorship.

The genuinely new scientific question is whether cross-scan agreement, on a
declared and sufficiently observed footprint, can distinguish a potentially
useful retention from a response warning alone. Its score, partition, thresholds
and numerical guard are proposed in the new design and await owner approval.
No prior authority is claimed for them.

## Exact input roles

[The machine input binding](EL_F13_BOUND_INPUTS_R0.1.json) records all absolute
paths, sizes, SHA-256 values, boundary identities and access roles.

The decision population is exactly six boundaries, 0–5, from the completed
EL-F12 H/uninjected trajectory. Each has its own verified compressed occurrence
spool, checkpoint, occurrence-ledger NetCDF and three array FITS maps: 36 files,
1,704,690,744 bytes. Their identities match the preserved EL-F12 output manifest.
Each ledger reports 12 scan markers and the 104-byte little-endian occurrence
schema. All map grids are 355×357. Only metadata and hashes were inspected for
this preparation; the new score was not computed and the spools were not
decompressed. Exact scan identities and accounting are future required checks.

The original decompressed-spool hashes and byte counts are bound by the fixed
H/uninjected scalar-repair receipt. An integrity reader may use those fields
only; the predictor receives no later outcome or earlier EL-F12 score from
that receipt. An implementation reference is not an additional data input.

Six existing outcome/report files are separately bound for reporting after
all predictions are frozen. They include both complete Half/Hold results,
the protection table, completion record and interpretation/manifest. They are
already exposed to the authors. Separation is an auditable dependency rule,
not a claim that EL-F13 is blinded or independent of development history.

The known empirical opportunities are few. H had one eligible a2000 key at
each of boundaries 1 and 2; no population is enlarged to create more examples.
The first-action contrasts can challenge a recommendation at boundary 1.
Later outcomes include earlier intervention effects and are not independent
per-key labels. Neither a population false-action rate nor a positive empirical
benefit rate is estimable from this packet.

No new raw/telescope/APT/fit-report input, observation, source injection,
reduction or replay is admitted. The legacy APT and historical-executable
limitations remain. No new experiment directory, scan-agreement helper implementation or
run configuration has been staged. The accompanying owner proposal is the
next significant decision; further work depends on its exact scope approval.
